destination.name: Warrumbungle National Park
destination.tagline: Spires, bluffs and dark night skies in the weathered core of a volcano near Coonabarabran.
destination.description: Warrumbungle National Park covers 23,311 ha of the Warrumbungle Range, the eroded remnant of a volcano near Coonabarabran, about 550 km north-west of Sydney. Walkers come for formations such as Belougery Spire, Crater Bluff and the Breadknife, which towers 90 m above the valley floor and is the park's most recognisable feature. The park was added to the National Heritage List in 2006, and in 2016 it became Australia's first certified Dark Sky Park. About 80% of it burned in January 2013, and walking tracks, campgrounds and visitor sites have since been rebuilt.
whyVisit: Walk the Breadknife and Grand High Tops
See the Milky Way over the range

goodToKnow.title: Pack for the High Tops
goodToKnow.detail: Bring water, a hat, sunscreen and food, and borrow a free locator beacon at the visitor centre for the High Tops loop.

goodToKnow.title: Observatory is a day visit
goodToKnow.detail: Siding Spring Observatory is open to visitors by day only, 8:30 am to 4 pm; for night viewing book a Coonabarabran Stargazing tour.

goodToKnow.title: Fee and roads
goodToKnow.detail: Entry is $8 per vehicle per day. The road from Coonabarabran is about 35 km to the visitor centre; the west approach via Coonamble has unsealed sections.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring a moderate climate and spring wildflowers, good for the High Tops walk and camping under the stars; summer often tops 30C with thunderstorms, and winter nights drop below freezing.

warrumbungle-1.bio: A 14.5 km Grade 4 loop from Pincham car park, climbing past Belougery Spire and Crater Bluff to the Grand High Tops and views of Bluff Mountain.

warrumbungle-2.bio: A working research observatory on Mt Woorut, opened in 1965 on the park's eastern edge, with a hands-on Exploratory, a cafe and a free AAT Visitor Gallery to visit by day.

warrumbungle-3.bio: The closest town to the Warrumbungles, about 35 km from the park visitor centre by road and 27 km from Siding Spring Observatory.
